$comment: The file shape behind a role's foundry.intake declaration. Modelled directly on @clossys/advisor's existing sponsor-question shape (SponsorQuestionCard, packages/advisor/src/sponsor-questions.ts): stable ids throughout, multiple choice only, and the recommended option listed first so a non-technical client is never asked to pick from an unordered list.

cardShape.id: string -- stable across versions; a role must never reuse an id for a different question
cardShape.prompt: string -- one sentence, plain language, the client can actually answer
cardShape.choices: IntakeQuestionChoice[] -- at least two; choices[0] is the recommended option (see `rule`)
cardShape.recommendedChoiceId: string -- must equal choices[0].id; explicit so a reordering by an editor cannot silently change the recommendation
cardShape.somethingElseFollowUp: string -- the one-sentence follow-up prompt when none of the listed choices fit

runtimeChoicesCard.$comment: Issue #1179: an extension for a card whose choices are only known at runtime, which a static intake file cannot express. Only an engine builds one; a role's static intake file never does. scripts/check-package-framework.mjs's validateIntakeCardsShape() enforces that: a static card and each of its choices are closed to the keys cardShape and choiceShape declare, `selection` on a card or `detail` on a choice is refused as intake-card-runtime-only-field, and any other undeclared key as intake-card-unknown-field.
runtimeChoicesCard.builtBy: @clossys/advisor's repositoryChoiceCard() (packages/advisor/src/repository-choice.ts): a list of repositories the agent gathers from GitHub for the client's sign-in and handed to the engine, never typed by the client
runtimeChoicesCard.selection: "many" -- the client may choose any nonempty set of the choices, not exactly one. A card without `selection` is a single-choice card, as every static intake card is.
runtimeChoicesCard.choices: Each choice id is the stable id of the runtime value it stands for (for the repository card, the repository's owner/name, which must satisfy docs/contracts/repository-inventory.json definitions/repositoryId). The `something-else` choice is always last. Because the values are supplied at runtime, a card may offer a single value plus `something-else`.
runtimeChoicesCard.recommendedChoiceId: Present, and equal to choices[0].id, only when the engine has evidence for one choice (for the repository card, the repository the client is working in, and only when it is on the list; a current repository that is not listed leaves the card without a recommendation, never refused). Absent otherwise: an engine never invents a recommendation, and the remaining choices are sorted by id so the client is never asked to pick from an unordered list.
runtimeChoicesCard.answer: The client's answer is the list of chosen ids, checked against exactly the ids the card offered (applyRepositoryChoice()): an id the card did not offer, or one chosen twice, is refused by position, never echoed.

choiceShape.id: string -- stable, unique within the card
choiceShape.label: string -- the client-facing option text
choiceShape.detail: runtime-choices cards only (see runtimeChoicesCard): optional supporting text for the choice, for example a repository's own description, cleaned by Unicode property class and capped by the engine that builds the card (@clossys/advisor's cleanDescription()); refused in a static intake file

engagementContext.readFrom: clossys/brief.json `context` (docs/contracts/engagement-brief.json) -- a snapshot of the hub's clossys/advisor/context.json, present in every staffed repository. A role reads it before presenting any intake card; an absent `context` means every field is unknown.
engagementContext.reservedIds: docs/contracts/engagement-context.json definitions.fieldId.enum -- business, product, audience, stage, intent, constraints. These are Advisor's context questions, identified by field id.
engagementContext.duplicateRule: A role's intake card may not ask a question the engagement context already answers. Matching is on stable question ids only: a card whose `id`, trimmed and lowercased, is one of the reserved ids duplicates that context field -- a case or whitespace variant is the same id, not a different question (card ids are lowercase slugs, `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, and the shape check reports any other). A role that needs one of those answers reads it from the brief's `context`; when the field is unknown there, the founder is sent back to Advisor's own context card for it (packages/advisor/src/context-questions.ts), never re-asked under the role's own card. A card asking something narrower (for example which audience segment to address first) uses its own distinct id and is not a duplicate. Prompt wording is deliberately not compared: paraphrase is a review concern, not a gate one.
engagementContext.enforcement: scripts/check-package-framework.mjs, rule `intake-card-duplicates-context-field`. Report mode (the default, and what CI runs today) prints it as a WARN line and never fails on it; --enforce promotes it to a finding, together with the rest of that gate's --enforce wave (issue #1172's sequencing). An unreadable engagement-context contract is reported the same way (`engagement-context-contract-unreadable`), so an enforcing pass never claims a check that did not run.

rule: A card's `choices` array is never empty and never has fewer than two entries. `recommendedChoiceId` names an id present in `choices` and equal to `choices[0].id` -- the recommended option is always presented first, never merely flagged. Every `id` (card and choice) is stable multiple-choice vocabulary: once shipped, a role package does not repurpose an id for a different meaning, because a consumer's prior answer is stored against that id and must keep meaning what it meant when it was recorded.
